Tech Scan: Harness

What should carry a task between model calls, and when does it need more than the managed harness? Compare the loop, tools, memory and checks without assembling an unnecessary stack.

Draft research reference from web sources reviewed 11–12 November 2026; not locally deployed or benchmarked. For the underlying explanation, read Concepts: harness engineering.

On this page
What needs to run the agent? Start with the managed harness When configuration is not enough Separate discovery from permission Sources

What needs to run the agent?

Choose the software that carries a task between model calls, supplies tools and checks the result. For an AWS workload, begin with the managed harness and add a separate component only for a requirement it cannot meet. The harness explanation in Concepts describes how these responsibilities fit together.[1]

Responsibilities to check before adding another product
ResponsibilityStarting point on AWSReason to investigate more
State and loopAgentCore managed harnessA required pause, transition or recovery path cannot be configured
Tools and authorisationExplicit tool selectors; AgentCore Gateway and Policy for calls routed through itA tool needs custom execution or an authorisation integration
ContextTask instructions and repository files; Bedrock Knowledge Bases when retrieval is neededThe task needs information absent from its supplied context
MemorySession state; investigate AgentCore Memory for retained recallA defined recall and retention requirement exceeds session state
EvaluationTask-specific test cases; assess AgentCore EvaluationsThe scoring or review workflow needs another implementation
ObservabilityCloudWatch and AgentCore ObservabilityRequired traces, cost attribution or investigation workflows are missing

The managed harness supplies the loop and tools; its configuration still needs explicit boundaries.[4][25] Retrieval can use Bedrock Knowledge Bases through an AgentCore Gateway connector when needed, rather than becoming a compulsory component of every harness.[12][13]

The MCP Registry supplies discovery metadata, not a replacement for AgentCore Gateway: finding a server does not execute or authorise its tools.[27] Gateway Policy governs calls through that gateway.[11] OPA needs an enforcement integration for runtime decisions; Conftest tests structured configuration. Neither is a drop-in Gateway Policy replacement.[30][31]

What this page does not cover:

  • Model choice (Tech Scan: Models)
  • Retrieval detail (Tech Scan: Context, planned)
  • The execution sandbox (Tech Scan: Sandbox)
  • Gateway routing (Tech Scan: Gateway)

Each is a separate spoke.

Start with the managed harness

Start with the AgentCore managed harness: a config-based, Strands-powered harness with an explicit approved model, individually allowed tools and bounded execution.[4][5] AWS records its general availability in June 2026.[6] Use managed Claude or OpenAI models through Bedrock; direct provider APIs are exceptions for a specific capability or approved-region gap, not the assumed route. Managed defaults can evolve, so default behaviour is not an immutable model or tool policy — record the exact model, tools and permissions you approved, and review them when the default changes.

For repository coding, use the managed harness's built-in shell and filesystem tools to read, write and edit files. Prepare the environment to clone a repository, run tests and commit changes; install tools such as git or use a custom image when required.[25][26] Code Interpreter is optional for Python, JavaScript or TypeScript data analysis and computation. Add Browser only for a specific browsing task.[25] The sandbox must hold six trust rules:[7]

  • Separate trust domains
  • Minimal execution roles
  • Explicit outbound enforcement
  • Approved dependencies
  • Protected credentials
  • Authenticated session ownership

Runtime Instances are not equivalent to per-session microVM compute: co-resident agents in an Instances session share a filesystem and can access each other's execution-role credentials.[8] Gateway policy governs traffic through the Gateway, not arbitrary shell networking. VPC attachment alone is not evidence of package-only egress — network access limited to approved package registries — or secret denial.[7]

Use Step Functions when an outer workflow needs any of these:[9]

  • Explicit sequencing
  • Retries
  • Parallel checks
  • Independently authorised human decisions

Keep that workflow separate from the model's per-turn tool loop. A framework implements that loop in application code; AgentCore Runtime is hosting for agent code, not a model-serving endpoint. The managed harness supplies an implementation so you need not start by assembling a framework.[4]

The optimised Step Functions InvokeHarness task is request/response only, has a 15-minute task limit and does not support task-token callbacks; a timeout does not automatically cancel the harness.[9][10] This is an integration limit, not a general absence of AgentCore approval support. Inline functions provide a human-in-the-loop pattern: the harness pauses at the tool call, returns it to client code and waits for a result. The application still implements the authorised decision and resume path.[25]

When configuration is not enough

Write down the missing behaviour before choosing a framework. Compare the same task, approval boundary and recovery case with the managed harness; a language preference alone does not establish that another runtime is needed.

Different reasons to investigate application code
Candidate and responsibilityTriggerEvidence and limit
LangGraph — stateful orchestrationA required graph transition or recovery path cannot be configuredThomson Reuters reports a LangGraph orchestrator using AgentCore; a customer-coauthored case, not an independent benchmark.[14]
AI SDK — TypeScript agent loopThe application needs code-level loop and context control in TypeScriptToolLoopAgent supports tool loops, context management and server-side state; assess persistence and recovery for the intended task.[28] For long-running work use WorkflowAgent in @ai-sdk/workflow (AI SDK 7, June 2026): durable agents with persisted steps, retries and approvals. ToolLoopAgent alone is in-memory and loses progress on a crash. The Edge runtime is deprecated; the SDK runs on Node.js and other runtimes, not edge-only.
OpenHands — coding-agent applicationThe requirement is an existing coding-agent workflow rather than a loop libraryThe upstream repository describes the application; deployment and tool permissions still need qualification.[15]

Using the AI SDK library does not require Vercel hosting. Its Amazon Bedrock provider can call Bedrock from the application's AWS environment; this library choice does not add a non-AWS cloud route.[29] Keep the approved model and individually allowed tools explicit whichever library supplies the loop.

Keep evaluation separate from telemetry. Define representative task cases and expected outcomes, then check whether the managed evaluation workflow fits them. For tracing, begin with CloudWatch and AgentCore Observability; Coding Agent Insights dashboards depend on expected telemetry names and resource attributes.[16][17]

Additional candidates: open after identifying a missing responsibility

The initial research named the following candidates. They are a shortlist for further research, not distinct recommendations: the evidence does not discriminate between products with the same trigger. Verify the current licence, release, deployment contract and AWS operating model before selecting a candidate.[22]

  • Loop libraries and frameworks: Strands Agents, CrewAI, Mastra, Pydantic AI, SmolAgents, Agno and LlamaIndex Workflows. Compare the required language, tool execution and state transitions rather than unmeasured speed or size rankings.
  • Memory: Mem0, Letta and Graphiti. Specify what is retained, how time affects recall, deletion and tenant separation before comparing them with AgentCore Memory.
  • Durable execution: Temporal, Inngest, Trigger.dev, Hatchet, Restate, DBOS and Prefect. Compare restart, duplicate-delivery, cancellation and approval-resume behaviour; a shared promise of long-running work is not a selection criterion.
  • Evaluation and observability: Langfuse, Braintrust, Maxim AI and Arize Phoenix. Compare scoring, trace export, access controls and retention against the missing workflow.

Langfuse publishes its own guide to deploying on AWS and reports an ECS Fargate deployment for its own application.[18][20] Its official Terraform module describes EKS/Fargate, a different deployment path.[19] Self-hosted software, a vendor's managed service and its own infrastructure are different evidence; none establishes the intended account's operating results.

Zep's 2 April 2025 announcement explains its shift from Community Edition to Graphiti; it is a migration context, not proof that Graphiti meets a new workload.[23] A secondary report about Trigger.dev's hosted tier is retained in its source entry; obtain the vendor's current advisory before using it for an adoption decision.[24]

Separate discovery from permission

Use the official MCP Registry to find server metadata, then review the actual server, tool schemas, authentication and deployment. Its current documentation labels the registry preview and warns of breaking changes or data resets before general availability. Listing a server does not make its tools trusted or approved.[27] The earlier third-party comparison of Glama, Smithery and Mintlify is retained as research history, not a required vetting layer or an automatic migration instruction.[21]

Check inherited integrations before extending them

The initial research flagged AutoGen, Semantic Kernel, OpenAI Assistants API and LangChain AgentExecutor for lifecycle review.[22] Those issue-level reports are not current primary-source lifecycle evidence. Before extending an inherited integration, check its upstream support notice, supported replacement and migration constraints; do not infer that every product in the group is retired.

What to establish before adoption

Ask the implementing engineer to run a representative repository task in the intended account. Retain the exact model, tool selectors, role permissions, environment image, task result, traces and full cost. Recheck those boundaries when a managed default changes.

  • Revoke a permission and confirm that the prohibited tool action fails.
  • Exercise a timeout, retry and restart; inspect duplicate side effects and cancellation.
  • Pause for an authorised human decision and confirm that denial does not resume the action.

For work beyond the InvokeHarness task limit, define how the outer workflow starts, observes and cancels the job. Exercise an inline-function approval separately from a Step Functions callback; the two resume paths are not interchangeable.

Next, compare the recorded results with the task's requirements and unresolved failures. Use Tech Scan: Sandbox to qualify execution boundaries; a functioning harness does not authorise release.
